synopsis: ERA guidance, together with EN 14363:2016+A2:2022 and DynoTRAIN, provides a standards-and-regulatory framework for rail running-dynamics validation; its WAG TSI application guide (GUI/WAG TSI/2023) accepts physical procedures or simulations with validated models as evidence [f8131, f7710]. Across Chapter 10 and the glossary, the guidance permits extending test conditions and modifying a validated model of a tested vehicle to assess a changed vehicle, including comparison with an approved reference vehicle [f7896, f7895, f7897, f15365, f14676]. The framework uses physical-data comparison sets containing at least 24 comparisons from at least 12 sections, retains physical running tests for the reference vehicle, and has an associated validation study using more than 1,000 simulations [f8133, f8136, f8134]. The corpus identifies this as the strongest family-transfer and test-reduction precedent for off-road automatic braking and the closest formal analogue to delta validation, but notes that the framework has no formal risk scaling [f8137, f7898, f8132].
